newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria says refineries fail to justify investment.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria says refineries fail to justify investment.

text.p: Big investments made on repairs of Nigerian oil refineries have not yielded tangible gains, finance minister Anthony Ani said in remarks published on Tuesday.

"Despite the huge amount allocated for the refineries, we have found that they have not been repaired, the result of which is persistent shortage of fuel in Nigeria, the world's sixth largest producer of oil," Ani said at a public lecture in Kaduna, northern Nigeria.
According to him, $440 million and $295 million were allocated to the Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) in 1995 and 1996, respectively for projects including refinery repairs.

Four refineries operated by NNPC around the country have a combined refining capacity of 445,000 barrels of crude oil daily but are currently producing at less than a third of their capacity due to deteriorating facilities.
This has caused bouts of fuel supply shortages that have intermittently plagued Nigeria since January.
"With sound planning and a good oil and gas policy, Nigeria should no longer be scandalised by the persistent fuel shortage as we have seen recently," Ani said.
